passage: Large lakes shape the climate of their shores. Because water warms and cools far more slowly than land, a lake gives off heat stored over the summer well into autumn, sparing nearby orchards from early frosts. In spring the same slowness works the other way: the still-cold water chills the shoreline air, holding back blossoms until the danger of a late frost has passed. For shoreline growers, the lake thus serves as their ______.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The lake warms the shore in autumn and chills it in spring, softening the swing toward frost damage in each season, so it serves as the growers' "cushion." A "blanket" fits only the autumn half, since a blanket keeps warmth in and would not chill the air in spring, while a "clock" fits only the spring half, where the cold water sets the timing of the blossoms; in autumn the lake times nothing, it simply releases heat. A "bellwether" would signal coming changes, but the lake does not warn growers of frost; it changes the temperature itself.
